summary: Red brick lighthouse on Agate Bay, lit April 1892 for Mesabi iron ore; run by the Lake County Historical Society; main beacon failed 2019, temporary beacon 2021, new LED beacon planned July 2025.

light.characteristic: Fl(2) W 20s (aerobeacon signature, 1921 onward: 0.4 s light, 4.6 s dark, 0.4 s light, 14.6 s dark)

lens.where: Lens returned to Two Harbors in 2015, on display in the keepers' quarters (LighthouseFriends)

structures.note: HAER: 49 ft 6 in (15.1 m) to the top of the ventilator ball; USLHS: 43.5 ft (13.3 m) to lantern centre

events.note: Congress appropriates $10,000 for a light and keeper's dwelling
Condemnation proceedings July 1890; deed to the United States within two months
Work begins 15 July 1891; finished in November
Put into operation 15 April 1892 (LighthouseFriends, Duluth News Tribune); Wikipedia's 14 April is not used
Fixed fourth-order Fresnel lens
Barn converted to an assistant keeper's dwelling; post light on the breakwater (separate station) established 14 December
Color of light changed from red to white, 10 April 1897 (Board)
Parabolic deflector on the fog signal house
Revolving four-sided lens replaces the original fixed lens (LighthouseFriends)
Kerosene changed to incandescent oil vapor
Second assistant keeper's post added to the station
Second assistant keeper (Hans F. Christianson, spelled Christensen on the roster) commended for helping in the rescue of two fishermen
Electrified (230,000 candlepower); fog signal changed to an air diaphone
Revolving lens removed and transferred to the Inland Seas Maritime Museum (LighthouseFriends); HAER gives 1970
DCB-224 aerobeacon: the society dates the beacon to 1969; it was repurposed from another lighthouse and installed in the late 1990s (society page)
Fog signal discontinued
Light automated; Coast Guard personnel stationed elsewhere
Coast Guard grants the society a lease (LighthouseFriends 1987; society page 1988 for tours)
Ownership transferred to the Lake County Historical Society by act of Congress (society: 1999; LighthouseFriends: 1998)
Lighthouse Bed and Breakfast opens
Society assumes responsibility for the light from the Coast Guard
Original Fresnel lens returned to Two Harbors and placed in an exhibit case
DCB-224 aerobeacon fails on 25 November 2019 and cannot be repaired; light dark
Non-functioning DCB-224 removed on 11 July 2020
Maxiluna-300 flashing beacon, on a five-year loan, lit 2 June 2021
New LED beacon, bought with $50,000 raised, planned for 4 July 2025 as part of the society's centennial (MPR 5 July 2025 report)

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends and the Duluth News Tribune both describe the rotating aerobeacon's signature as two 0.4 s flashes in each 20 s (the 1921 electric light, replaced 2019-2021). The record's 5 s period matches neither. The current 2021 loan beacon is a flashing light, so the characteristic should be checked against the current Light List before the record is changed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends and the Duluth News Tribune give 15 April 1892 as the day the light was put into operation; Wikipedia's 14 April is a lead only and is not cited. The story uses 15 April.
HAER says the original lens was replaced in 1970; LighthouseFriends says the revolving lens that had replaced the original in 1907 was removed in 1969. The story gives both as the sources' own dates.
The historical society says 1999, by a bill passed in Congress; LighthouseFriends says 1998. The story gives both as the sources' own dates.
The 1912 Bulletin names Hans F. Christianson; the roster lists Hans F. Christensen in the same post for 1912 and 1913. Not confirmed as the same man.

notes_for_editor: Roster matched to the USLHS place by name and position (0.55 km), printed verbatim. The 54 roster lines are used with person slugs; LighthouseFriends' keeper list matches them apart from the spelling 'Pederson' (one line kept, the other dropped). The HAER form is NRHP 84001483's data pages (Hyde, 1979) and is readable through the NPGallery PDF; it is the only primary source for the building's dimensions. The Board reports for 1891, 1894, 1895, 1896 and 1897 are OCR. The 1891 site paragraph is read from two scan pages; the OCR garbles the words 'satisfactory result', so the story paraphrases that phrase. The 1896 barn sentence has a hyphen broken across words ('con- verted'), so the story quotes only the clean phrase. Conflicts: first lit 14 April (Wikipedia lead) against 15 April (LighthouseFriends, Duluth News Tribune); lens removal 1970 (HAER) against 1969 (LighthouseFriends, society); ownership transfer 1998 (LighthouseFriends) against 1999 (society); the MPR 2025 report says the light was built in 1893, against 1891-92 in the other sources (not used). Second assistant 1912: Bulletin says Christianson, roster says Christensen, same post and year; the story says the sources do not say whether they are the same man, and gives both spellings. The relight: MPR (5 July 2025) and the society's calendar say the new beacon was to be lit on 4 July 2025. The story says 'planned', because no source read confirms the lighting itself. The society's own page (undated copy) still shows the 2021 loan beacon. Check before printing. Newspapers: a Chronicling America search for 1892 gave nothing relevant. Wikipedia was used for leads only. The 'Two Harbors, Michigan' Bulletin entries (1915, 1916) are a different place and are not used. The Lederle name also appears at Muskegon (a fourth assistant in 1903); not linked. Access: LighthouseFriends' tour hours may be out of date; the society's page does not give hours. The Lighthouse Bed and Breakfast is a public business. No person living is named except as a public role (the Bulletin's keeper names are historical).
